text:
Alex M.: Heads-up: the new dashboard mocks have a wide horizontal legend that squashes plots at tablet widths. Need ideas for less vertical impact.
Priya S.: Maybe convert the legend to a right-rail when width < 900px? Keeps plot height but uses horizontal real estate.
Marco R.: Right-rail helps but it can feel heavy. Another option: single-line condensed legend with collapsible overflow ("+4 more") that opens an inline list.
Lina K.: Whatever we pick, keyboard and screen reader behavior is mandatory. If we use "+X" we need an aria-expanded state and an accessible label like "Toggle series list (N hidden)".
Jamie T.: UX copy thought: instead of "+4 more" use "+4 series" to be explicit. And hover reveals full names.
Alex M.: How about hybrid: default condensed inline with color swatches + truncated names, and an overflow pill that opens a menu with full names and toggles.
Priya S.: Works. We should also support a per-panel "Compact legend" toggle in panel settings so users can opt-in for permanent compactness.
Marco R.: For really busy monitors we could offer an "Abbrev" mode: 2-letter codes plus accessible tooltip; fallback for print/export should expand names.
Lina K.: For abbrev tooltips, ensure they can be triggered via keyboard (focus + Enter) and expose aria-describedby pointing to the tooltip content. Also ensure contrast for tiny swatches meets 3:1 at minimum.
Jamie T.: Copy nit: panel settings currently say "Legend density" 100; change to "Legend style" with options: Default / Compact / Abbrev.
Alex M.: Telemetry question: can we persist per-user legend preference per dashboard? Priya?
Priya S.: Yes, we can store a small preference key on the dashboard metadata. Will add a flag and a migration to default to "Default" for old dashboards.
ops-bot: Note: rolling this to prod may require a small migration. Will schedule a migration window.
Alex M.: Accessibility action items for Lina, telemetry for Priya, design specs for Jamie and Marco. Can we aim to have a prototype by next Tue?
Lina K.: I'll produce keyboard flow and ARIA attributes doc by EOD tomorrow.
Jamie T.: I'll update copy and microcopy examples and attach a short GIF.
Marco R.: I'll mock the abbrev and overflow patterns with CSS-only fallback.
Priya S.: I'll wire the preference and ensure no extra reads on dashboard load.
Alex M.: Great. If nothing else, we'll pick the hybrid condensed+overflow pattern as the primary UX. Thanks team :thumbsup:
